quest.title: A Toast to Victory
quest.description: The operation to save Lesser Lord Kusanali has concluded. Despite the many surreal experiences that ensued, you feel surprisingly calm after waking up again in bed, facing the rising sun.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x850, Mora x34150, Silver Twig x1, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #Good morning, {NICKNAME}! Looks like you're awake.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep yep!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I prepared some breakfast today. Please have a taste! I hope you'll like it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's nice to have you here so we can eat something yummy!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Well, now that I've recovered from Eleazar, I'm feeling better than ever. I can even prepare four or five meals a day now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Paimon bets they're all delicious!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You enjoy a yummy breakfast with Collei, who's been waiting for you...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #Oh, by the way, {NICKNAME}, someone brought a letter for you after you went to sleep last night.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon hasn't already read it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, Paimon wanted to read the letter with you after you woke up, so Paimon didn't open it. Alright, let's read it now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's from Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem~ "We're going to hold a feast at the Grand Bazaar and celebrate Cyno's reinstatement as the General Mahamatra!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "As heroes of Sumeru, please be sure to attend. I'll wait for you." The date of the banquet is written on the back... It's in two days.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, I've also heard that you've become heroes here as well. That's amazing!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Everyone's aware of your abilities, there's no need to be modest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's go to the Grand Bazaar to have a look!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh, before you leave, be sure to inform Master Tighnari.

choices.text: We were just doing our part.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Sometimes I'm really envious of strong and confident people like you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But you're amazing too, Collei.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh, you're embarrassing me... Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari~!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Good morning. How do you feel today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We feel much better. How about you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's your wound, Tighnari?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm recovering well, thanks for asking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But from the looks of it, you seem to be already busy with work again.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's fine, I'm not that busy, really.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Eleazar patients have recovered, as well as Haypasia. For now, I only need to tend to my Forest Watcher duties.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems once Irminsul started getting better, everything else started to recover, too!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, but there are still some residual effects.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Withering is one example. Though it won't spread anymore, the existing zones won't just disappear. We Forest Rangers will still need to do the work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I appreciate that's a lot to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, we have some good news. Cyno got his position back!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Heh, this news is hardly new. He had already mentioned it to me before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean he was already here? Why didn't he come say hi to us...?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: He visited once, but he was afraid of disturbing you while you were resting. He just asked me a few questions and left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then you probably already know all about the celebration feast!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Celebration feast? No, I haven't heard anything about that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... But didn't Nilou say in her letter that they would celebrate Cyno? He didn't tell you?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm, perhaps... or, alternatively, he doesn't know about it, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Come to think of it, Cyno doesn't seem like the type who'd enjoy a celebration feast.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess Nilou's only planning on telling him once festivities are underway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You and Collei are both Cyno's close friends. Why don't you come to the feast with us?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei has taken over some of my tasks these days. I don't think she'll have time for it... not to mention me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You see, some "VIPs" have come to the forest recently.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? VIPs? Very important Paimons?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, technically speaking, they are former VIPs. The sages involved in recent incidents have begun their training in the Avidya Forest, and the people they had previously imprisoned have all been released.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is your master all right?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes. He's a little weak, but he isn't injured and his condition is stable.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali in her boundless mercy has decided to spare Azar and the other wrongdoers. Supposedly, they were ashamed of their shallow ideologies, and have decided to dedicate the rest of their lives to cultivating wisdom in the Avidya Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: When they learned that Lesser Lord Kusanali had defeated The Balladeer and saved Irminsul, they were shocked at first, but also became happy, feeling that the sacred light guiding them on the path of discovering wisdom had begun to shine once again.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As a result, work has increased for the Forest Rangers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds really exhausting...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: There's nothing we can do, really...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But that's another topic. Back to the matter at hand — are you two planning to head out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, right! We're here to request permission to head out. Would that be... okay?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You've recovered well. You may go, but be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! Will do!

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: ...Well, there won't be any problems if the feast starts at that time. Everything has already been prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Mr. Zubayr, I've finished tallying things up here! Well, except for the guests...

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: *sigh* Is a simple reply really that much to ask of our guests? It's affecting our arrangements.

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: It'll be fine... Besides, it never hurts to get things ready in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Haha. I was thinking the same thing. The feast will be held sooner or later, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Nilou~!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We got your letter, so here we are!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You're the best. The other guests haven't even replied yet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are we the only ones that have arrived?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yeah, I had someone deliver letters to all of our guests, but maybe everyone is still busy with other things.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: Look, I get it, Sumeru is in an extremely important period of transition right now, but even if your friends are important figures, they shouldn't just ignore your request like this.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: Nilou is Sumeru's number one celebrity, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Of course, you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: Hehe, you have no idea how happy I am to talk to people with good taste.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you consider enjoying Nilou's dance as having good taste, then almost everybody has good taste!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because Paimon thinks everybody will love her performance.

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: That's right! We all think she's amazing, too.

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: Nilou is an absolute favorite among those of us who frequent the Grand Bazaar. For outlanders, you have a great eye!

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: Master Zubayr, let's have a vote for the most outstanding audience members next time. I think these two may win!

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: Nonsense. It is not for us to determine the value of an audience.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: But indeed, we could try giving gifts to people with particularly good taste... I heard there's a device in Fontaine called a "Kamera" that can record people's appearances as pictures. Such pictures would make superb gifts...

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: Ooh, good idea! I wonder where we can find one...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Haha, you guys are so funny. There's really no need for that. I'm satisfied just being able to perform here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's always a lot going on at the Grand Bazaar.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yeah, and that's why I love it here.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, could you help confirm if the letters were actually delivered?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: If for some reason they didn't receive the letters, then please tell everyone that there will be a feast here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, we'll go around and check.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we can also check out how everything in Sumeru is going now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know where everybody is?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hmm... When I wrote the letters, I heard that Dehya was in Port Ormos, and Alhaitham was at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: As for Cyno, we've only heard that he appears at the Akademiya from time to time...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I'm not too sure about Rahman's whereabouts. My guess is that he's with Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: As for Dunyarzad, I just hope she's feeling better... I sent her a letter, but I was afraid of disturbing her. If you have time, please ask about her for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Okay, got it. Let's go, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Inquire about Alhaitham's whereabouts in the Akademiya

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... we haven't seen Alhaitham anywhere. Let's ask that person over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem, hey there! Have you seen Alhaitham around?

dialogues.speaker: Geoff
dialogues.text: Yes, it seems Scribe Alhaitham has gone to the House of Daena. You should be able to find him there.

dialogues.speaker: Geoff
dialogues.text: But, you're already the second group of people I've seen looking for him today. He must be quite the busy man.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Who else was looking for him?

dialogues.speaker: Geoff
dialogues.text: Mr. Kaveh was just here asking about him. You wouldn't believe how terrible their relationship is... and now you two are here...

dialogues.speaker: Geoff
dialogues.text: Don't tell me everyone's here looking for gossip about the sages?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, not at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way, we're strictly here on business!

dialogues.speaker: Geoff
dialogues.text: *ahem* Ah, I see. Sorry, I thought maybe everyone's as interested in rumors about the sages as I am...

talks.objective: Enter the House of Daena and look for Alhaitham

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alhaitham should be around here somewhere, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, he's over there! But it looks like he might not have time for us...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's already talking with someone else.
Just put down that worthless book and tell me what happened in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This is not just some worthless book. Do you have any idea how difficult it is to find a physical book like this in Sumeru?

It doesn't matter, it's probably just another thing that you used your authority to get your hands on anyway. Just put it aside. Listen, I came back today only to hear that the sages have disappeared!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Oh? You sound surprised. I thought you would already know the inside story.
Would I be here asking you if I knew? You're the Scribe, not me. So just tell me what you know already!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, I almost became a sage.
Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Don't sound too surprised now. You're the renowned Kaveh, light of the Kshahrewar. Besides, as a master builder and craftsman, chances are you'll be appointed as a sage, too.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Hmph. Why do I feel like you don't really mean it?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmph, what makes you say that? Why would you question my heartfelt sincerity?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Maybe it's because you've never said anything good about me before.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yeah, well, I share a similar sentiment. And anyone who knows you as well as I do would surely do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ugh, you...!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: See!? This is why I hate discussing anything with you. Your ridiculous and arrogant attitude always gets in the way!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hm, it seems that you really can't stand my personality.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hah, what was your first clue?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, then you might as well move out of my house.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Are you threatening me? Stooping to a new low, I see!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ugh, and don't change the subject. You? A sage? What a joke. The Akademiya might as well just close tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Are they... having a fight...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's see how this plays out. We're not in a rush, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Forget what's going on with the Akademiya, haven't you been busy with your construction project? Tell me, when are you going to build yourself a mansion?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Don't get me started... I get angry just thinking about it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So, what great building did our master architect work on this time?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Like I need to tell you! Keep your nose out of my business.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No, I think we deserve to know. Where were you when Sumeru needed you most?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I was in the desert for a large project, but considering Haravatat's utter ignorance of architectural and aesthetic matters, you probably wouldn't understand.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Which is truly unfortunate! I can only pity the man who doesn't understand the first thing about beauty and romance. Unlike a true...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hold on, wait a second, what do you mean by "when Sumeru needed me most"?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, while you were out fiddling around in the desert, many people came together to save Sumeru from a crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hah, and you think I'd believe that?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Look, all you really need to know is that Azar and all his accomplices have all been overthrown.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? What nonsense are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's no skin off my nose if you don't believe me. It's not like my Darshan was the one trying to apply for funding from the Grand Sage. Yours, though, on the other hand...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You know what? I'll ask around! I'm sure someone knows what's going on here. You're dead if I find out you're lying to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Alhaitham!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're running some errands for Nilou. Have you received her letter?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Letter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou said she sent out a letter inviting everyone to a celebration feast in two days at the Grand Bazaar. We'll also be celebrating Cyno's reinstatement as General Mahamatra.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If she addressed the letter to "Alhaitham of the Akademiya," then the letter should have gone to my office.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I've been busy these days, so I haven't had time to check for any new mail at my office. I only now have some free time to attend to personal matters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you always been so busy with your work?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Of course not. I'm only busy these days because several sages have been dismissed recently, and the whole Akademiya was practically turned upside down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari told us they all went to train in the Avidya Forest. Apparently they'll spend the rest of their lives there.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That is already the best possible ending for the likes of them.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Four of the Six Great Sages were possessed by their desire for power and attempted to create a new god. In order to pull it off, they even imprisoned the other two rational sages. To imagine such things could take place in the Akademiya... I don't know where to begin...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "The Six Great Sages"... sounds pretty powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're right. Huh, it feels kinda strange to hear them called that after all this time... But then again, the "Six Great Schools" sounded pretty impressive, too.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes, at least that's how they're supposed to sound.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's said that when the Akademiya was first founded, the Dendro Archon herself established the Six Great Schools, each representing one of the six different types of wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Numerous Darshans have sprung up and faded. Only the Six Darshans, attaching themselves to the Six Great Schools, have stood the test of time and obtained permanent seats in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Now, the Six Darshans are nearly synonymous with the Six Great Schools, and the leaders selected for the schools are the Six Great Sages.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Among the Six Great Sages there is one central leader, the Grand Sage.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, only the sages from Vahumana and Amurta remain now. They were imprisoned for opposing Azar and were only rescued after Azar's downfall.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So who's managing things in the other four schools now? Do they need to find someone new?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes. Normally, new sages are selected based on a strict set of criteria.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, didn't you just say something about becoming a sage? If they pick you, then we'd have a huge connection in Sumeru!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon has a point!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes, about that... *ahem* You didn't let me finish my sentence.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The person in charge of personnel affairs nominated me to be the Grand Sage in place of Azar and help Lesser Lord Kusanali manage the Akademiya, but... I refused.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? But... Why!? Ugh, can't you be a little more ambitious?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm not even interested in being one of the Six Great Sages. Like I said before, I don't like being a leader.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, all right. So are you busy these days trying to find others to take the job?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's not my job, either. I'm only responsible for handling important affairs within the Akademiya before the new sages take office.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're still a leader now, even if it's just temporary.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hah, and the first thing I'll do is reject Kshahrewar's application for funding.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, who was that other person just now? Is he your friend?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do we look like friends?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't know! That's why Paimon's asking!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: His name is Kaveh, my roommate. You could say he's the representative for Kshahrewar scholars.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He didn't seem to believe a word you told him.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Which is exactly why he always has so many problems.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So everything that's happened recently must be a huge change for the people of Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for your hard work these days.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Such is the work of the Akademiya Scribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well anyway, no matter how busy you are, since you were our planner, remember to attend the celebration feast in two days!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: All right, I'll see you there.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The House of Daena is the last quiet place in the whole Akademiya now. I was originally planning to stay here a little longer...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But there's a chance that Kaveh might show up again... Tch, what a nuisance. I'd better go somewhere else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is Port Ormos, now where could Dehya be...?
Is that Paimon I hear?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It's been a while, how are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad! It's been so long since we've seen you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're good. How about you?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I'm doing well. I can go as far as saying I've never been happier in my entire life!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I don't know if you've heard, but Eleazar has completely disappeared, and all the patients have recovered.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You kidding? Knowing them and the connections they've got, I'm sure they've heard about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Didn't expect to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's right. My lady is feeling better now, so I'm accompanying her for a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Why do you still call me that, Dehya? You've already informed my father of your resignation.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, I guess I'm just used to calling you "my lady." Old habits die hard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Resignation? You mean you're quitting?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah, I might start losing my edge if I keep being a bodyguard for the Homayanis.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: You know that my parents and I are fond of you and that we appreciate you very much. It wouldn't be a problem if you wished to continue to be our bodyguard.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, I'm not a woman that's easily persuaded. You should know that by now, my lady.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: When I took this job, I had already decided that I'd quit as soon as you recovered. It's time for me to get back out there and chase that horizon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what're you gonna do now if you're not gonna be a bodyguard anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I want to take a risky job and put my body to the test again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But we literally just finished one of the most dangerous jobs ever. Are you getting bored already?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I know. If I hadn't joined in that plan with you, I wouldn't have come up with this idea.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I guess I still get fired up by that feeling of going all-out in a fight... It made me realize that I'm still a mercenary through and through.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Life is short, and I'm happy I got to be a part of that operation.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But the whole thing also made me realize that there are still many problems in Sumeru, and as a desert-dweller, I'm still not completely ready to settle down on this side of the wall.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Well, I remember a friend had someone bring you a message...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You mean Alhaitham? Haha, I didn't expect him to still remember that. I thought he was joking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We just came from talking with Alhaitham at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Did he tell you that he suggested that I come work at the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We didn't hear anything about that.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I heard that Azar and his cronies fell from power, and Alhaitham told me that now was a good time to find a job in the Akademiya, but only if I wanted to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Paimon can't see you being anything other than a mercenary.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hehe, me neither. But I think Dehya would look great dressed up as a scholar.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Bleh, forget about it. I wouldn't last ten seconds in there...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alhaitham probably just liked the way I worked and knew I'm good in a fight, so he suggested I find some work in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you know, if you take him up on the offer, Cyno might actually agree and let you become a matra.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because you're super amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha. The matra have all the talent they need as long as they have Cyno. I prefer to be free to live however I choose.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: In fact, I chose this job from the very start because I knew it'd be right up my alley.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: ...Even if being a mercenary means facing all kinds of danger?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: A lion has to return to the wild sooner or later. If anything, being your bodyguard has been unfamiliar territory for me.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I don't want to see you go... But I'll respect your decision.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm glad to hear you say that.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: C'mon, no need for the sad face, it's not like we'll never meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess being free is just a part of how Dehya operates.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Once the whole Dendro Archon thing has settled, everything in Sumeru will take a turn for the better. That makes me happy, too.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But a peaceful society will probably mean less demand for mercenaries like me. Before long, we'll be a dying breed, so I'd better get to work while I still can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But wait a second, you make it sound like you're leaving now!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, no... not yet, at least. I promised my lady that I'd stick around until next week.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So have you been in Port Ormos this entire time? We were wondering if you had received a letter from Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh, did Nilou write to us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She heard that you were seen in Port Ormos, so she sent the letter here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It was probably sent to the inn that we're staying at.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady has been very energetic lately and keeps taking me on hikes, staying out even into the night. By the time we get back, the receptionist is usually off napping on the job.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Right, and we tend to leave quite early in the mornings, so the old man on duty is also usually dozing off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what it really sounds like is that the person on duty is always asleep.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I bet the letter's at the reception desk. I'll go check later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder there wasn't a reply, you never received the letter. Good thing Nilou asked us to come and check on that.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry to make you two come all the way out here.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It must be something important for Nilou to specifically write to us like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, she said they're preparing a victory feast in the Grand Bazaar, and we'll also be celebrating Cyno's reinstatement as General Mahamatra. She was hoping you could come.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Great. I'll be sure to attend!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Count me in, too. But is there some sort of dress code or anything for the feast? Can I just show up looking like this?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Since it's being organized by Nilou, I don't think she'll be too picky about that. If anything, I think she'd want to see us as our most natural selves.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alright, then this is how I'll show up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The feast will be held in two days, so don't forget!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for letting us know. We'll see you there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way, do you happen to know where Cyno and Rahman are?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The General Mahamatra always comes and goes without a trace. Normally, no one knows his whereabouts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But last time we met, he mentioned he had something to do in Aaru Village. You can try your luck there.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: As for Rahman, your guess is as good as mine. I only remember he said that he had something to discuss with Cyno... You can ask Cyno when you meet him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. You'd better get going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, on to our next stop!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while since we last visited Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, there's Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We recovered well, and Tighnari agreed to let us leave, so now we're out and about again!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It seems Gandharva Ville's medical treatment is still as good as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, and Tighnari is recovering well, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's good to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for taking us to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're the one who brought us to him when we lost consciousness, right? Thanks for that!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're welcome. Tighnari has excellent medical skills, and Collei is quite attentive. It was the best place for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why are you just standing here like a dead tree?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm meeting some people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Candace?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I've already talked with Candace and the village chief. They're still at the usual place. You can go there if you'd like to see them.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But you know one of the people I'm meeting as well.
Oh? By King Deshret's blessing, my friend suddenly appears in the desert. Don't tell me you've run into trouble and need us to help now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rahman! And... huh? Setaria?

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Oh? You... know me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, well... You're pretty famous in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Don't worry, these are our friends. No need to be so guarded.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: ...I see.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How have you been doing lately?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I'm doing well. Many good things have happened recently.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Same here. Really, I feel that my whole life has started to shine after suddenly finding a new direction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, tell us everything!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Yeah, you go ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Alright, well I suppose I should start by saying...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: I've decided to leave the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not going to be a scholar anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: It's not that I've given up on being a scholar... Instead, you could say I've found a new identity.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: I will no longer pursue research like a typical scholar, but I have not completely given up on my relationship to knowledge either.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Haha, I can see what you're saying now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: I plan to leave the Akademiya and return to teach here in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so you want to become a teacher?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Setaria will return to support education here and teach people from the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: She can't teach everyone on her own, but there are many of us Eremites all over Sumeru. She came to discuss a collaboration with me and hoped that I could bring her ideas to the Eremites.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Yes, it's my hope that the Eremites can help me select a group of smart people with the best aptitude for teaching. I'll teach them, and after they've finished learning from me, they can go educate more people.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: That is the true meaning of education and spreading of knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: The people of King Deshret suffer from sandstorms, exile, and ignorance. Miss Setaria is more than welcome to come teach here. Her arrival is like a star shining in the desert night.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: The stars have always guided caravans, thieves, soldiers, and travelers who get lost in the night. They lead those in the dark out of trouble and back to safety.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Oh please, where's all of this coming from? I'm starting to feel a little embarrassed...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: You deserve these compliments. Mercenaries are accustomed to danger and don't fear death, which is why we recognize extraordinary actions that common people would easily overlook.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Setaria's idea will bring much good to many people.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: At first, I feared it was destined to fail... Everyone knows that the Akademiya doesn't allow scholars to teach in the desert without permission.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: As you know, all knowledge is under their surveillance and control, and very few desert-dwellers are as lucky as me...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: But what I heard at that time has been haunting my heart, as if there were lightning bolts constantly bombarding my soul.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: "Setaria, you tread a treacherous path, and the longer you ignore it, the tighter the Akademiya's grasp on you will become..."

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: "Setaria, why haven't you gone home?" "Never forget that the desert that belongs to you lies elsewhere."

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Miss...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: These words sparked something in me, and I knew that I had to bring something back to my people after going home.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: I gathered up the courage to approach the Grand Sage, only to find that he was no longer at the Akademiya. Lord Cyno told me that Azar didn't belong there anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Azar has received much-needed punishment, though if you ask me, it may have been too light... *sigh* You probably have already heard.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, we heard.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Lord Cyno helped me obtain permission to leave the Akademiya for the desert, and accompanied me here to discuss collaboration with members of the Eremites.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: My plan was able to go smoothly thanks to him and Rahman.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're all doing so much for the desert!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Aside from that, I also have some other business to discuss with Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali has allocated many resources to support and develop the desert. I've done some business for her, and part of it required the assistance of the Eremites.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I applied for a few batches of educational materials from the Akademiya and sent them to several groups in the desert, as instructed by Lesser Lord Kusanali. I believe the people will make good use of them.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: That's exactly what the people here need. Physical books and other related items... If it weren't for Cyno and Lesser Lord Kusanali, I'm afraid we'd never be able to get our hands on them.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Apart from this, the Akademiya is also recruiting scholars that are willing to teach in the desert. I'll let you and Setaria know as soon as I have any more news.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We must be persistent about this and maintain these resources to ensure long-term effectiveness.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: This is the first time in hundreds of years we've had a glimmer of hope. I think this may be the turning point for the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Remember these words? "Here lies our faithful priest, Kasala. His wisdom is a miracle among the people, deserving of high praise and admiration."

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I hope people with wisdom like that priest will rise again among the desert-dwellers... then we'll once again see the wisdom and glory that once shook the world.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Enough about us, are you here to discuss some business, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, not at all! We're actually here on behalf of Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou wanted to write to everyone, but she wasn't sure where the letters should be sent, so she asked us to come find everyone personally.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A celebration feast will be held in two days at the Grand Bazaar. She hopes that all of you would be able to attend.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: At the feast, we'll also be celebrating Cyno's reinstatement as General Mahamatra!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although uh, judging from your appearance, it seems you've already been reinstated... Paimon thought you would only start working for the Akademiya after the feast.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Celebration... feast?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh? So you really didn't know?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's the first I've heard of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari was right, he really didn't know...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Hahaha, this feast is for you, Cyno. Sounds to me like you'll have to be there.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: It's rare to see that kind of expression from Lord Cyno... You must not like feasts very much.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No, not really, but I'll go.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You two are invited as well!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I still have a lot to handle here. Besides, I need to look after Miss Setaria in the desert, so I'll have to pass.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I won't be able to join you. Although, if you'd be so kind... please give a message to Miss Nilou for me.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: ...The message is...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: "I'm sorry for how I treated you before, but now I understand the beauty of your dance. It's like a light shining in the sky."

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: "You and the art you symbolize are not only beautiful, but also lively and powerful, so much so that it was prohibited."

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: "Please keep dancing, and someday, I'll be able to appreciate your art in person."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we've got all that down!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll be sure to give the message to Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Our job here is complete as well. Cyno, remember, party's in two days! Make sure you're there!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Got it.

talks.objective: Wait for the feast to start (19:00 – 24:00 two days later)

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: I'll go to the Adventurers' Guild later and ask Miss Katheryne if she knows how to get one of those Kameras.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: Yes, please do. I'm sure the audience would be thrilled at the chance of receiving commemorative gifts.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: It could be our special surprise that we prepare for everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I think it's an amazing idea! Who knows, if we take more pictures, they might even become the signature souvenir of the Grand Bazaar.

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: And Nilou will become even more famous, haha! It won't be long till people are fighting for front row at your performances.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: I've heard that this Kamera is not just something anyone can use as they please. It must be aimed properly and subjects should pose for the best results.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ah, should we get ready then? Perhaps we should wear something a little more appropriate...

dialogues.speaker: Hushang
dialogues.text: No, no, I think we look absolutely fine! If anything, when we pose for this... uh, clever invention, we should just be ourselves, hm?

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: You really think so...?

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Bazaar to attend the feast

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everybody's already here. Looks like we're the last ones to arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ah, there you are!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good evening.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, look who finally decided to show up.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: You look like you came here immediately after finishing up some work. I'm very happy to see you here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we're not late, are we? It's just that everyone else arrived ahead of time!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I propose that the last one who arrived be put in charge of today's speeches.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Nah, there won't be any speeches today.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Oh really? Well, even better.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Come join us over here! Let's share some great food and drinks, and chat about all sorts of fun things.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Everything looks quite good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wow... Paimon can't wait! {NICKNAME}, just look at all the delicious food here!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The feast and celebration of the General Mahamatra in the Grand Bazaar goes as planned. Drinks are flowing, the food is delicious, and the venue is beautifully arranged.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everybody eats and drinks before enjoying the performance prepared by Nilou and everyone in the Grand Bazaar...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Time passes gradually in the wonderful atmosphere, and the beautiful evening feels almost like a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa~! It's so delicious! Oh~! This grilled meat tastes amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The food was specially prepared for you by everyone in the Grand Bazaar, and we have gifts that were sent by the residents of Sumeru City when they heard we were holding a feast.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Everyone that came said that you saved Sumeru, and wanted me to thank you all on their behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Feels kinda nice to be seen as a hero. I could get used to this.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Being a bodyguard is also a hero's job! You've always been amazing, Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, my lady sure has a way with words. Thanks, I'm glad to hear it!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: And I'm happy to meet everyone that participated in the great plan.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, we've really done something impressive together... It's unbelievable!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We owe it to our abilities... and luck.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Really? Why do I remember everybody thinking that luck was against us and feeling like we hardly had a chance of succeeding?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's how I remember it, too.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's luck that brought us together and it was luck that let us form a team. Then it took even more luck for us to formulate a plan and implement it successfully.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Moreover, judging from the results, everything worked out well.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yeah, everyone gave it their all when it mattered most.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: It was almost like a performance. We took the stage and put on our best show.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Everyone played their part, and thanks to everyone's efforts, the performance was a great success.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So would you say we're good actors too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's one more talent under our belt.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: It's such a blessing that Lesser Lord Kusanali was able to return to power at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Yes! Even after being abandoned and neglected so many times, she has finally returned.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Return to the Akademiya? Abandoned and neglected...?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, Lesser Lord Kusanali once used all her power in a great disaster, which resulted in her losing all of her wisdom and memories of the past. The Akademiya basically abandoned her because of it.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: This should be something everybody should remember... Huh, you look surprised... I didn't say anything wrong, did I?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No, everything you said is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Whew, that's good.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah {NICKNAME}, what's with that face? You knew all of this already!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't mind me, my... my mind was elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *ahem* Even if those two giants of the Akademiya are here, I still have to say it...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Those sages really have some nerve. Five hundred years ago, Lesser Lord Kusanali used all her power for the people of Sumeru, and what did they do in return?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It seems that after everyone forgot Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, their understanding of Sumeru's history also changed...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Now everyone believes that Lesser Lord Kusanali has been Sumeru's archon all along.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe I'm the only one in all of Teyvat who remembers that Greater Lord Rukkhadevata ever existed.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (As the witness of all that happened, I shall respect her choice and keep the secret for her.)

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If you bite the hand that feeds you, then don't act surprised when it turns into a knuckle sandwich, right, Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Perhaps I shouldn't say this, but their treatment of Lesser Lord Kusanali calls for a more severe punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You could simply tell Lesser Lord Kusanali that you wish to have Azar and his accomplices severely punished.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...I respect our deity's decision, and won't interfere in any way.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: While we're on this topic, why didn't you accept the Akademiya's invitation to become the Grand Sage?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Are you trying to say that I'm fit to be a sage?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Heh, not at all, but every person handling the selection process has said that you are the most suitable candidate to lead the Akademiya right now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Why? Because he dethroned Azar from power?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: *ahem* Could you try to put it another way? This is a good thing, yet you're making it sound like I overthrew Azar for my own personal gain.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But seriously though, I always wondered if you had some personal motives behind it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I did have my own motive, but it had nothing to do with being a sage.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If the rules of our nation were suddenly cast by the wayside, then it wouldn't be long until chaos ensued. I had no intention of letting their dreams disrupt my life.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: By that, you mean your life working as the Akademiya's Scribe?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Precisely.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, is that all?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's the only reason why you joined us and came up with all those plans?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's reason enough.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: You've certainly got quite the personality...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You flatter me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alright then, how about you? You've already resumed work as the General Mahamatra, right?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Will you be happy with that life?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...It's not about being happy. There are merely a lot of things that I must do.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Even so, keep your spirits up and try to be happy, okay? And try to smile more every day, just like I'm doing now.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Thank you. I'll keep that in mind.

talks.objective: Talk to everyone at the feast

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, the grilled meat over there is delicious. Have you tried it?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Yes! I also tried some fruits just now. They're very sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: What an amazing place to relax. No wonder everybody likes to rest at the Grand Bazaar.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You said it. Oh, look who else is here.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hello, I'm so happy Nilou invited everybody. Now I have a chance to meet all the heroes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My pleasure, I'm glad we could come.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, less of that polite chit-chat and more eating and drinking. The feast is about having fun, not stuffy formalities!

talks.objective: Talk to everyone at the feast

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I seldom participate in such lively gatherings, but the atmosphere here is quite good.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh. I thought you might find it boring.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No, this gathering today has a unique meaning.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Grand Bazaar is lively because the people here feel happiness from the bottom of their hearts, unlike the farces at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That happiness is an emotion that'll be forever alien to those bookworms who have driven themselves insane by studying.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...Hm, I seem to have taken both keys when I left the house.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Heh, oh well.

talks.objective: Talk to everyone at the feast

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #Ah, there you are, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Well, how is it? Are you enjoying the feast today? If there's anything you're unhappy with, just let me know. I'll be sure to take note of it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's great, thanks for inviting me.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hehe... That's good.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: It's the first time I've ever invited so many exceptional people to one place. I was a little nervous myself.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You see, every guest here is quite extraordinary. It's unbelievable that we got everyone to gather here... almost like a fairy tale.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Make sure you live it up tonight! I'll be happy as long as you're enjoying yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We have a message to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Setaria's message to Nilou...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I'm honored to have her think of me this way. If I have a chance in the future, I would really like to invite her to one of my performances.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #I can't explain why, but I just feel elated right now! Thank you, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Talk to everyone at the feast

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The atmosphere here is good, and everything is delicious.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It must be rare to see you at such a lively gathering.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I don't often come to such places, but it feels quite good.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I have a lot to handle these days. Otherwise, I could show you around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's alright, don't worry about us.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's always next time. We're friends, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...This feast is pretty good. I like it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's wrong? Your head is starting to droop...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you can't just fall asleep here! Paimon will go find something delicious for you to eat. You'll wake up once you've put something yummy in your tummy!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course. Just wait here for Paimon!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Is it because I didn't sleep well last night that I feel sleepy all of a sudden? Or is it because I'm too full...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh? It seems like someone is there...)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, it's me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Nahida, it looks like my consciousness is connected to yours again.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mhm. You may blame me for being a bit too self-indulgent. I was thinking about talking with you, and the next thing I knew, I had made a connection with you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The connection between us is amazing! It's like flora and the fence it grows upon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Is there anything you need from me?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I heard there's an amazing celebration feast today at the Grand Bazaar. I wanted to have a look for myself, so I snuck in.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Lately, I've been so busy dealing with all the fallout from recent events, so I really haven't had any free time...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, although you've already helped me with a lot, there's still one more thing I hope you can help me with.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What is it?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Please say thank you to everyone for me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Ah, so that's what this is about... Nahida, it'd be better if you could do that yourself.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh... Is it not convenient for you to do that for me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Some things in this world must be done by yourself.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But, if I just show up all of a sudden... people will become all quiet and stiff, won't they?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: What if I end up scaring them and ruining this wonderful feast... That'd be the last thing I want.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It'll be fine. Please don't worry too much!)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm... Let me think about it...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Okay!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Have you made up your mind?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, I have.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That's good... Wait? Huh!?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You said I should go thank everyone as myself, right? So...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've decided to borrow your body for the time being. Please don't blame me. The flora also climbs up the fence to get closer to the sky.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Then at least promise me you won't say anything weird when you're in my body!)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Everyone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you awake now? Paimon was just about to bring you the food!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that voice... Nahida!?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: #Hold up! What's going on, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I didn't expect to have a conversation with the consciousness of Lesser Lord Kusanali in the Grand Bazaar. Interesting. Is this also a part of the feast?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: No, no, of course not! Are you... Lesser Lord Kusanali?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hello, Nilou.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: You know who I am!?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, I already know every one of you. Nilou, Alhaitham, Cyno, Dehya, Paimon, and Dunyarzad.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Lesser... Lord Kusanali...?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #I took the liberty of occupying {NICKNAME}'s body so that I could thank all of you in person.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thank you so much for rescuing me, even if that meant placing your own safety in peril, and taking the risk of becoming enemies with the Akademiya, the Sages, The Doctor, The Balladeer, and even the entirety of Sumeru.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Without you, without any of you... I would have been in a much more difficult situation.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Had you not helped me to resolve the crisis, not only I, but Sumeru and even the entirety of Teyvat, would've suffered great misfortune.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: People refer to you as "the heroes who managed to rescue a god." I am quite fond of this name. It not only explains your identities, but also bears witness to your relationship with me.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Please allow me to present to you my most sincere gratitude.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali, y—you've done so much for Sumeru, and I... I didn't even have a chance to do anything for you... You don't have to do this.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Dunyarzad, the suffering you endured during your illness is also proof of you being with me and praying for me. Thank you.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You don't need to be so ceremonious... It's always been my duty to protect you.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: This is how the relationship between the Akademiya and Dendro Archon should be. We just did what was necessary and set things back on the right path.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: You're an archon, but you act so humble. You really don't need to be so polite with us.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I... I'm honored to have been able to take part in this plan! I hope you liked the dance I dedicated to you!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Thank you, all of you. Thank you so much.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (See? Just like I said, everybody is very happy to meet you.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Yeah!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Nahida shows up for a surprise visit and brings the feast to its climax. Sincere joy flows in the hearts of everyone present.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: A warm atmosphere of talking and laughter carries on late into the night...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: And the feast ends on a perfect note.

choices.text: Feels like I'm about to nod off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you awake? Did you rest well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think... I slept alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After Nahida left, you ate a lot of food. You've become a glutton!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Still nothing compared to Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph. That just means you still have a lot to learn from Master Paimon, the Sage of Gluttony!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All right. Since you're awake now, should we go and have a chat with Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She should be in the Akademiya right about now. If you have any questions, now's your chance to ask.

talks.objective: Go to the Sanctuary of Surasthana

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: What a fantastic night. I'm still immersed in all the happiness and joy, like a candle floating on water.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So are we, and that's why we're here to talk with you!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Is there anything you want to know?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: After recent events, the Akasha can no longer function as it used to.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've given it some thought, and have decided to shut it down permanently.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But this is definitely not a bad thing. Even from the beginning, I've been planning to shut it down.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The Akasha's centralized administration of knowledge has always restrained people's curiosity and curtailed the number of paths available to them. I don't think this is good for Sumeru.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Although people may initially feel a little uncomfortable with the loss of the Akasha, they will soon understand that this life is more suitable for them.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And as for the future of Sumeru... I'm preparing to regain control of the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The former sages have received their punishment, but the new sages have yet to be selected. I will oversee the process personally.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I hope that the new Six Great Sages will be more focused on academics. Sumeru needs such leaders more than ever.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The other big issue is the people of King Deshret — all the residents of the desert, in fact. They have been mistreated for far too long.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've already taken some measures to address this. It will take some time to rebuild everything, but no matter if it's culture, friendship, or trust... we will rebuild it.

choices.text: About what happened after I fell asleep that day...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You mean, what happened after The Doctor put you to sleep?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did he take the Gnoses?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You guessed correctly... The top-ranked Fatui Harbingers, up to No. 3, possess power comparable to that of gods. I was no match for him in that kind of situation.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: However, in spite of the bad situation, I still managed to make a fair deal with The Doctor.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm sure you remember the entity that changed your fate — the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: In fact, the Heavenly Principles has been quiet since the Khaenri'ah disaster five hundred years ago. I used this point as leverage against The Doctor.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I told him that the Heavenly Principles may be awakened if I destroyed a Gnosis. Although it was just a bluff, he still fell for it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I assumed that the Heavenly Principles wouldn't just stand by and let such extensive damage to its "laws" take place.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And as for what I exchanged for the Gnoses...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The exchange served as both punishment for The Doctor, as well as a boon of new knowledge that I couldn't refuse as the God of Wisdom.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm sure you probably want to ask what that knowledge was... Please forgive me, for I can't tell you that right now, but I believe you'll discover it one day.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: He's still in a coma. I've hidden him like how one would hide a feather.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I know you have many misgivings about him, but as someone who had "become a god," he has retained a number of very useful features.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Don't worry, I'll keep an eye on him and make sure he doesn't do any evil.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: In addition, there are still some mysteries left in him. Some things may be very clear from my perspective, but he has still yet to understand them himself.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: His future will be determined by fate.

choices.text: About Fontaine, the next stop on my journey...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Is that where you're headed next? Fontaine, the nation of justice.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As far as I know, that nation operates on a judicial system.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does their archon personally judge people?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: No, there's a Chief Justice in Fontaine. Generally speaking, the Hydro Archon, Focalors, won't preside over individual trials.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: However... even then, Focalors will still make herself present at just about every trial. It seems that she just likes to immerse herself in that sort of atmosphere.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As archon, she still reserves the right to influence the final verdict.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, let's just say she's got... hmm... a very unique personality.

choices.text: I've got nothing else to say.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Are you sure? Isn't there something else that you haven't asked about yet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You mean...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #About... your {M#sister}{F#brother}.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #While you were resting at Gandharva Ville, I took some time to perform an Irminsul search for information on your {M#sister}{F#brother}.

choices.text: But... we both came from beyond the sea of stars.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah, isn't Irminsul a repository for all the information and memories of Teyvat? So there shouldn't be anything on {M#him}{F#her} or {M#his sister}{F#her brother}.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #This is true in your case, {NICKNAME}. Irminsul indeed does not have any information on you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: However...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #There must be something different about your {F#brother}{M#sister}... because as it turns out, the world has recorded information on {F#him}{M#her} after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #There's only one possible explanation: {M#She}{F#He} belongs to this world.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(How is that possible? We journeyed the sea of stars all our lives until we came here. How could {M#she}{F#he} possibly hail from Teyvat...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(Things don't add up. Is there something wrong with my memories? Or is it this world that has done something to {M#her}{F#him}...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... nothing about this makes any sense. Wasn't this your first trip to Teyvat?

choices.text: Do you have any further intel?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: According to the records I was able to access, your sibling suddenly appeared in Khaenri'ah...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #After the Khaenri'ah disaster, {M#she}{F#he} began {M#her}{F#his} journey through the seven nations of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #But just as {M#her}{F#his} journey was about to reach its conclusion, the Irminsul records on {M#her}{F#him} suddenly become fuzzy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you mean, "fuzzy"? Did something happen to {M#her}{F#him}?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #All I know for sure is that somebody, for reasons only they can know, is deliberately obfuscating {F#his}{M#her} fate...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And whoever it is... if they can do that, who knows what else they're capable of.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could it be related to... the Abyss?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But even that wouldn't explain how {F#he}{M#she} somehow comes from this world...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Something else I noticed was that according to these records, the Fatui have not classified your sibling as one of the "Descenders."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Descenders?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What's a Descender? Paimon's never heard of it...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Look, I'm sure you must be curious about the information I received from the Fatui in return for my Gnosis, right?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: A very important part of the intel was about this world's Descenders... external beings, ones that don't belong to this world.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you are Teyvat's "Fourth Descender."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Fourth...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh!? So the Fatui count three other Descenders before {NICKNAME}? And {M#his sister}{F#her brother} isn't even one of them?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's right. My current hypothesis is that the "First Descender" was likely what we now call the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As for the other Descenders... I still need to verify their existence. It could take me some time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew... Paimon's head's about to burst from all this crazy new information...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And yet, even knowing all this, I'm sure you must still have a lot of unanswered questions. I must say, I truly regret that I can't help you more as the God of Wisdom...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: There are many questions in my heart as well. I will need some time to go through each one of them.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Same here... I'll need some time to reflect on what you've said.

choices.text: #Do you know what {M#she}{F#he} has been through?
#There shouldn't be any information on {M#her}{F#him} in Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Everything has been getting better lately, and my mood has been improving as well.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You can come find me anytime if you need anything.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for looking after us.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You're welcome, I was just doing my duty. Remember to talk to Master Tighnari before you leave.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's Haypasia?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah yes, thank you for remembering her. She continued her training in the forest after she recovered. As a scholar, she never slacks off.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Great.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A lot has happened lately. Collei and I have been busy, but don't worry, we'll take care of ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As for Cyno's reinstatement, the more I think about it, the more I suspect that he just doesn't have a single clue about this feast.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But this does remind me that Collei and I should find an opportunity to celebrate him as well. He has helped me a lot during this time.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And you as well, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Take care. Please find me if you need anything.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Azar has gone to the Avidya Forest to reflect on himself for the rest of his life, and those people say they want you to replace him as the Grand Sage? What have you done!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa, Azar's downfall is of his own making. What does it have to do with me?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Everyone out there is saying something different. Some say Azar wanted to create a god, while others say he wanted to sell his power...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Heh, but none of these sound very likely. If you ask me, I think the people spreading rumors around here don't have access to any real information.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Really? Then I'm sure you can use your abilities to uncover the truth for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Can't you show just a little respect to your senior and explain what's going on!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You were out there all this time and yet you still haven't managed to learn a single crucial bit of information. Heh, I'm impressed.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Fine. Apart from the leaders of Amurta and Vahumana, all the sages have been exposed and removed as Azar's accomplices. We need to select new sages for your Kshahrewar Darshan as well as my Haravatat Darshan.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What? Did my Darshan collude with Azar as well? Wait... could this be why they sent me out on a project?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Oh, I think that's just a coincidence. Besides, whatever you were doing won't have any significant impact now or in times to come.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You... Hmph! Listen here, I'm not buying any of it. Don't try to use this as an opportunity to talk about your crazy theories.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I think there are a few details that everyone is overlooking... For example, how as the Scribe, you were somehow able to escape this political crisis completely unscathed...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: This can easily be seen as the results of a power struggle, no? Yet nobody has stopped to point that out yet... I almost feel like I should go out and start telling people about that!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Be my guest, but I think everybody will be more interested in your own well-known gaffes.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Do you know what? I am done with you!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: After recovering from Eleazar, everything seems so different to me. When I look at the scenery I've visited before, it has a completely different feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah, you need to be stronger than an ox to take life by the horns.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I think I've heard you say something like that before, but today, I finally understand what you mean!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Is there any place you'd like to go? I can accompany you, I've got time.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hmm... What if I tell you I want to go to the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Fine by me!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If we go to the desert, I can introduce you to my friends there. But we should prepare and get everything we need before setting off.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Let's go! I'll go pack my luggage now. After we're done with the feast in two days, we can go have fun in the desert!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You can count me in!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Anyway, our preparation has been going smoothly these days. Can such good things really be happening in the desert? It's almost hard to believe...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Yes, even if you can't bring yourself to believe it, you should at least believe in those of us who are working hard to make it a reality.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Indeed. Take it one step at a time. There is still a long journey before you.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Haha, what heartwarming words.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, it's good to see you again. Cyno said you were resting in Gandharva Ville for some time. How are you feeling now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've fully recovered now.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Good to hear. I'm happy that you've returned safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Thanks for all that you've done. The villagers won't be exaggerating when they say, "Heroes once passed through our village."

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If you ever have time, please come visit Aaru Village again. I still want to go hunting with you.

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: Behold, everyone! Allow me to present you with our best show ever!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The next day...
